question: A 2021 model found escape to space too slow to have dried out early Mars. Where does it put the rest of the water?
options: Bound into minerals in the crust
answer: Bound into minerals in the crust. Reacting with rock, water was locked into clays and other minerals, taking up, by the model's range, 30% to 99% of the early water. Escape alone cannot match both the amount lost and the heavy hydrogen left behind. Much of the ocean may sit in the rocks.
move: Before saying something escaped, check whether it was absorbed where it stood.
ask: Before I say something escaped, have I checked whether it was soaked up where it stood?
trap: Pointing to the polar ice, the water everyone has seen in pictures.
reference: Scheller, Ehlmann, Hu, Adams & Yung, Long-term drying of Mars by sequestration of ocean-scale volumes of water in the crust, Science, 2021
